ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a piece of clothing with weight G is hung on an isosceles clothes hanger. It is known that the top angle of the clothes hanger is $\theta=120^{\circ}$, the base is horizontal, and friction is neglected. Find the magnitude of the force exerted by one side of the clothes hanger on the clothing.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the image, it can be seen that a piece of clothing is hanging on a hanger; the left and right sides of the hanger are roughly symmetrical, forming an isosceles shape; there is a hook above; the clothing is supported by the left and right sides of the hanger. The problem statement gives the vertex angle θ=120°, the base is horizontal, and friction is neglected. Then reason: Let the magnitude of the force exerted by one side of the hanger on the clothing be N. Since friction is neglected, the force exerted by the side of the hanger on the clothing is a support force perpendicular to that side rod; also because the hanger is isosceles and the clothing is in equilibrium, the support forces on the left and right sides are equal in magnitude. The vertex angle is 120°, so the two base angles of the isosceles triangle are both (180°-120°)/2=30°, that is, the angle between each slanted side and the horizontal base is 30°. The support force is perpendicular to the slanted side, so the angle between the support force and the horizontal direction is 60°. The horizontal components of the two support forces on the left and right cancel each other, and the vertical components together balance the weight G of the clothing, so there is 2N sin60°=G. Solving gives N=G/(2sin60°)=G/√3=√3G/3.
